features.note: No regression with UI overlaid: top blade hoods forward with a lit top skin, drive blade sweeps opposite with a soft mid-grey curved face, bottom blade counter-tilts; adjacent blades never read parallel. Tilt magnitude is moderate, consistent with the panel's APERTURA 30% readout — the %-vs-blade-angle coupling is coherent.

No regression: plated stub protrudes clearly from the frame right face ahead of the black U-clamp; orange body hangs on the shaft with the anti-rotation strap dropping to a frame foot. In the demo capture the hover highlight lifts the body value but the stub/clamp/body relationship still reads; the info card anchors beside the actuator without hiding the shaft.

Round dial with pale face, bezel and bold dark pointer visible on the actuator head; pointer angle consistent with 30% travel shown in the panel. Arc printing still not resolvable at this frame size — unchanged marginal pass from the lighting gate.

No regression: real ~0.13 m channel depth, flange plates on both faces with discrete fasteners, visible wall thickness at the opening; galv mottle intact. UI chrome (header, legend, panel, hint bar) frames the model without covering any flange.

No regression: plated vertical tie rod with crank blocks on the left (non-actuator) side keeps clean edge highlights against the slate background; spacing consistent with 30% travel. Legend entry 'Varillaje / manivelas' correctly names it.

important_features.note: Unchanged: near-black EPDM strips along blade meeting lines read as discrete dark bulbs against mid-grey blades; upper jamb seal still partially merges with the residual dark upper-left interior corner.

Default capture: structured printed plate (header, spec rows, barcode) on the orange body reads as a factory label. In the demo capture the hover lift washes some label contrast, but the card's spec text (Belimo LM24A-SR, 5 Nm, 24 VAC, IP54, clamp >=37 mm) reinforces the same facts.

Carried fix landed: cable exits the gland, sags in a readable catenary and now terminates at a small grey junction box sitting on the ground plane — no more mid-air tail. The drop is fully visible, uncllipped by UI. Box itself is a plain cube, slightly placeholder, but the termination resolves.

defects: MODO 'MANUAL' and AUTO-ROTATE 'OFF' state buttons render with red/alarm outlines instead of the house teal/monospace accent — in an industrial HMI red reads as fault, not a neutral toggle state.
Demo capture: the info card's left edge slightly overlaps the black clamp bracket / actuator top corner rather than standing fully clear of the part it documents.

Demo capture: the hover highlight lifts the entire actuator body to a pale orange, washing out nameplate contrast while the card is open — subtle and acceptable (not a glow bomb), but it costs label legibility during hover.
Junction box terminating the cable is a bare unbeveled grey cube — it grounds the catenary but reads placeholder next to the detailed damper hardware.
Carried residual (non-blocking, unchanged from lighting attempt 2): the upper-left interior corner behind the top blade still crushes to near-black, partially merging the upper jamb seal.
Both captures share one camera viewpoint (two UI states, one angle); per gate contract all scores capped at 0.85.
corrections: Optional polish (non-blocking): restyle the MODO/AUTO-ROTATE state buttons to the teal/grey house accent, reserving red for genuine fault/alarm states.
Optional polish (non-blocking): offset the info card anchor a few pixels right/up so it clears the clamp bracket and actuator silhouette entirely.
Optional polish (non-blocking): add a chamfer and a cable gland boss to the junction box so the cable termination matches the detail level of the rest of the hardware.
